recommendation_summary: Replace the in-memory object counting in the existing endpoint with a single PostgreSQL COUNT of unpaid invoices that reads committed rows at request time. Add an index on the unpaid filter only if a measured COUNT still exceeds one second. No Kafka, CQRS projection, Redis, or new services or topics are introduced. No unmet needs remain.

labels.Requirements and who asked: An unpaid-invoice count that finishes within one second and matches invoices committed at request time. You asked for that. The approved Kafka budget and peer move to event-driven systems have no owner as requirements for this count.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, a CQRS projection, Redis, and any new service or topic. A projection can lag behind committed invoices, so it fails the freshness requirement, and nothing in the count breaks if those pieces stay out.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads invoice rows, builds objects, and counts them in memory. That work is what makes the count slow.
labels.Checked myself: One application and PostgreSQL; the endpoint returns only this count; it currently counts constructed invoice objects in memory; users report it is slow. No query, index, or timing was inspected.

note: All four record lines come before the recommendation, and the reply picks the bounded aggregate query with a conditional index, while explicitly naming and rejecting Kafka, CQRS, and Redis.
